title: THE QUIET SCHOOL OF HIGH WENDEL
deck: Forty children under nine have stopped speaking at school in High Wendel, and a cable car, a clinic and a board vote each claim to know why. Illuminara cannot hear what a child chooses not to say, so she asks the question nobody has asked: is the channel they speak through clean?
shape: Six scenes over five days and a first snow three weeks on: a school gate where a mother and a doctor disagree, a classroom where the heroine becomes a bad student, a machine hall where an engineer demands to be shown the sound, a noon test written down in advance, a night of repair with stated limits and a safety check, and a yes that goes up like a hill.

scenes.title: Five Days
paragraphs: *High Wendel, the school gate · Monday, ten past eight, four days before the board votes*

The cable car crossed the sky above the gate every eleven minutes, a red cabin against thin cloud, and nobody in High Wendel looked up at it any more. In February an avalanche had shut the pass for eleven days. The car that opened in April had been built so that nothing would ever shut the town in again.
A woman in a freight-shed jacket stood at the gate with a six-year-old by the hand, and she did not let go when the bell rang.

**Sabrina**  
I'm Sabrina Vedd. I pack the bread that goes up on that car, six days a week, so don't think I came to ask you to switch it off.

**Sabrina**  
In March this one said li forty ways before breakfast. Now she looks at me and does her face. That's all. She does her face.

**Illuminara**  
Tell me one of the forty.

**Sabrina**  
Yes. It goes up at the end, like she's calling the dog.
The girl looked at the ground, at the gate, and at Illuminara, and said nothing at all. Her name was Nessa. She had her mother's chin.
A thin man with a folder under his arm had been waiting for the pause, and took it.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Pavel Orsolya, the school's physician. I would like to be brief and polite, and I can manage one of those. Forty children under nine, every one of them silent in class within the same six weeks. The nurse screened their hearing and all forty passed. The speech therapist who comes up from Dessau on the first Monday of the month has seen nine of them and found nothing in the ear, the mouth or the tongue. In February the mountain came down and the pass was shut for eleven days. Children keep their fear until it is safe to put it down. April was the first safe month.

**Sabrina**  
They talk at home. A bit. In the back rooms, with the door shut.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Which is exactly what fear does with a safe room. And here is the harm I am trying to prevent. The reading assessments are in six weeks. A child who will not read aloud is held back a year, and a held-back child of seven learns that the school is not for her. The clinic at Dessau can watch them every day. I cannot, and the therapist manages once a month.

**Illuminara**  
Does every family have to agree to Dessau?

**Dr Orsolya**  
In my proposal, yes, and each child asked as well, where a child can be asked. On Friday the board votes on a draft that says placement and parental notice. I did not write those words, and I did not get them struck.

**Sabrina**  
They'd take her on a notice.

**Dr Orsolya**  
They might. So on Friday I will oppose the wording and recommend the observation. Both. It is an unpopular position and I hold it.

**Illuminara**  
What would show you that you were wrong?
He considered the question as though it were a patient.

**Dr Orsolya**  
A forty-first fact that fear cannot explain. I have looked and I have not found one. If you find it, bring it to me before Friday and I will read it. I will not enjoy it.

**Illuminara**  
I would like to sit in their room for one day and ask them for nothing.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Ask them for nothing. That much I will gladly sign.

scenes.title: A Bad Student
paragraphs: *The little room, High Wendel school · Monday, half past ten*

Illuminara had learned all four thousand words of Wenn overnight. The tones were another matter. A tone is not something you know; it is something you do with your voice, and the one syllable li meant river if it stayed level, sorrow if it fell and yes if it rose. Her voice could do anything, which was the trouble. It had no habits to blame.

Before she sat down she did something she did not usually do. She turned her hearing down to the range of an ordinary teacher, so that she would not be the only person in the room who could hear what the children could not. It felt like walking with a hand over one eye.
The room was warm from the stove. Twelve children sat on low benches in a silence so well-behaved it was almost a courtesy. Nessa Vedd sat in the second row.
The teacher, a quiet man named Daan, asked whether anyone would like the window opened. Nessa raised her chin and said one syllable, with a small bright lift at the end of it.
Illuminara heard river. Level and flat, a word for a thing that was not in the room.

The teacher heard river too. He tilted his head and told her, kindly, that there was no river in here, and some of the others smiled with him. It was a very kind smile. Nessa's face closed like a door on a hinge, and she said nothing more that morning.
*She said yes,* Illuminara thought. *I watched her chin go up. I heard something else.*
Four more times before the noon bell a child tried a word and was answered with something that did not fit it, and each time the child looked at the floor a little longer than the time before.
At noon they ran down to the garden below the school, and the silence broke the way a river does when the ice goes out.

The garden was loud. It was full of li, rising, falling and level, thrown from child to child like a ball, with whole sentences chasing it. Nessa stood on the wall at the bottom, bossing a boy about a bucket.
Illuminara sat on a stone beside her and, being a polite guest, tried a word. She said li, meaning yes, and let her voice go where she thought a yes should go.
Nessa put the bucket down and laughed so hard she had to hold on to the wall.

**Nessa**  
That's sorrow. You said you were sad. Yes goes up. Up, like a hill.

**Illuminara**  
Show me which hill.

**Nessa**  
A little hill. Like Gran's, behind the church. Not a mountain. You're doing a mountain.
Illuminara did a little hill. Nessa judged it with her head on one side, said it would do, and explained at length why the bucket was hers.
*They talk down here. They stop at the door.* She carried that sentence up the garden path like a full cup.

At the school door she let her hearing open all the way, and the floor spoke. A single flat note was rising through the stone, no louder than a kettle at the back of a house and as steady as a held breath. It sat exactly as high as a six-year-old's voice. Under every word said in that building it drew a level line, and a level line is what a river sounds like.

scenes.title: Show Me the Sound
paragraphs: *The upper station, machine hall · Monday, half past two*

Ines Kallas had designed the cable car at a kitchen table in a valley that would not fund it, and she looked at Illuminara the way she looked at a frayed strand. The great bullwheel turned behind her, enormous and almost soundless.

**Ines**  
So you're the one who says my machine is eating children.

**Illuminara**  
I think your machine sings, and I think the children's voices live exactly where it does.

**Ines**  
My machine is quiet. Fifty-one decibels at the school wall. That is a library.

**Illuminara**  
A library is not a note. Your gearbox has a mesh tone at about three hundred and ten hertz at cruise, and a second one at six-twenty. A man's voice sits beneath it. A six-year-old's sits right on top of it. In Wenn the glide of the voice, up or down, is the whole difference between yes and sorrow, and a glide drawn over a steady note of its own pitch is a pencil line on a pencil-grey wall. They say yes in that room and are heard saying river. Nowhere else.

**Ines**  
At fifty-one decibels.

**Illuminara**  
Loudness isn't what hides it. Sameness is.
Ines said nothing for as long as it took a cabin to leave the platform.

**Ines**  
You want me to stop the only road this town has on the strength of a theory about sound. I was on the pass in February with a shovel. I know what it costs when the road is shut. Show me the sound.

**Illuminara**  
I'm not asking you to stop it. I'm asking you to let me show you, and to write down first what would prove me wrong.

**Ines**  
Written where?

**Illuminara**  
On a card, signed by the three of us, before anyone hears a word.

**Ines**  
Fine. And I run my own sweep on my own instrument. I don't take anyone's ears for a frequency, yours least of all.
She carried a spectrum trace to the bench and held it under the lamp. Two spikes stood in it, narrow and clean, at three-oh-nine and six-eighteen.

**Ines**  
A peak is not a child.

**Illuminara**  
No. That's the other half. At the noon rest the car is held for the rope check, and for twenty minutes there is no note. I'd like to play the same words in both halves, and see who hears what.

**Ines**  
Twenty minutes is all you get. Not twenty-one.

scenes.title: The Noon Rest
paragraphs: *The school hall · Tuesday, two minutes before noon*
The card had been signed the night before by three people and sealed in an envelope on the piano. Illuminara read it aloud, so that nobody could say they had not heard its terms.

*Eight listeners, in two panels of four, in two rooms. The twenty-four recordings, twelve children's and twelve adults' saying the same words, are split into Set A and Set B, six children and six adults in each. Panel One hears Set A with the drive running, before noon, and Set B with it stopped. Panel Two hears Set A with it stopped, and Set B with it running, after the rest. So every voice is judged by four listeners with the drive running and by four others with it stopped, and nobody hears a voice twice. A voice is misheard in a condition when three of its four listeners write a word other than the one its speaker meant, as the parent who asked has written on the back. If, with the drive running, more than three of the twelve children's voices are misheard, and with the drive stopped no more than one, and the adults are heard correctly both ways, we call it masking. If not, Illuminara says so and drops it. Dr Orsolya adds: this does not rule out fear. Ines adds: nothing here touches the car.*

Fourteen families had been asked for a voice note from the spring, before the car, and each child had been asked first. Two had said no and had not been asked twice. The twelve who agreed sat in the envelope beside twelve adults saying the same words. Nessa had told her mother, in the back room, that her yes-to-the-dog could be played once, and she sat at the back of the hall with her arms folded. Nobody had asked her to say a word.

Six parents, Ines and Dr Orsolya sat with slips of paper: Panel One in the hall, Panel Two in the little room across the passage, a speaker in each. Illuminara did not vote. She drew the order of each set from a hat, and every listener wrote river, sorrow or yes.

Panel One's first block ran with the car running. At noon the cabin stopped at the platform with a long sigh, and the note went out of the floor like a held breath let go. Illuminara felt it go in her own breastbone. *If the slips come back flat,* she thought, *I have put forty children's week on a hunch.* For the twenty minutes of the rest both rooms listened at once, Panel One to Set B and Panel Two to Set A.

At twenty past twelve the car moved off and the note came back into the floor, and Panel Two began its running block, Set B. She counted the slips twice, with Ines and Dr Orsolya at her shoulders, and read the results in the order she had promised.

**Illuminara**  
Children, drive running: seven of twelve voices misheard. Children, drive stopped: none. Adults, running: none. Adults, stopped: none.
Nobody spoke. A cabin crossed the window and went on up the mountain.

**Ines**  
Order.

**Illuminara**  
Panel One heard the car running first and then stopped, Panel Two the other way round. Each set was heard both ways, by different people in opposite order, and each panel's own slips show the same split: the running block misheard, the stopped block clean. Here are their sheets.
She laid them on the piano beside the envelope. Ines read them the way she would have read a weld.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Seven. And none. Then I have spent four months listening to forty children through the wrong wall.

**Illuminara**  
Or through a wall that nobody knew was there.

**Dr Orsolya**  
I would like that to be a comfort. It is not yet. This does not tell me whether they are also afraid.

**Illuminara**  
No. We can't know until the wall is gone. Then you'll hear what is left, and you'll be the one to answer it.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Then take it down. I will find out what is left.
Ines had filled in her own sheet like everyone else, and was now staring at her own trace.

**Ines**  
Three-oh-nine. I called that note smooth for two years. I tuned that gearbox with grown-up ears.
She folded the paper in four.

**Ines**  
I'll fix it. Don't thank me.

scenes.title: Four Percent
paragraphs: *The upper station, machine hall · Wednesday night, ten past ten*

Ines had asked the town for the night. Eleven hours without its one road was the price, and she had named that first. She worked with the car held from the last evening run until nine in the morning and a crew of five, and she explained as she went, because she had decided that the town would not be mended by anything it could not follow.

**Ines**  
Three things. An isolation mount under the gearbox, so the rock stops carrying the note up the ridge. A tuned absorber on the casing, for the note itself. And four percent off cruise speed, because the school floor is a drum, it rings at three-ten, and I'd like the note to arrive where the drum isn't.

**Illuminara**  
What does four percent cost?

**Ines**  
A ride is thirty-eight minutes. Four percent is a minute and a half. You get that and not a second more.

**Ines**  
And here are my limits, so nobody wonders. Tension, brake and rope I don't touch, for you, for the board or for God. Mounts and speed are mine. And here is what puts the old mount back: the coupling outside the maker's alignment limit, the gearbox shaking harder than it did last year, or the car taking one metre longer to stop. Any one of the three and the rigid mount goes back tonight, and you can all be cross with me.

**Illuminara**  
I wouldn't want you to do anything else.

At six the sweeps ran, hers and the valley inspector's. He had driven up in the night with a thermos and a distrust of enthusiasm, and he had come to check that the repair had not touched what it must not touch. The two traces lay one on the other like a signature and its copy. The note at the school wall was down by twenty-six decibels, and nobody could find it in the floor.

Then came the part nobody would put in a story. The coupling sat inside its limit. The gearbox shook less than it had the year before. At seven the car ran up empty and came down empty. At eight Ines ran the emergency stop from full cruise with a cabin of sandbags, and the inspector, who had expected to find fault, wrote the stopping distance down and looked at it as though it owed him something: inside the certificate, with half a metre to spare. At nine the first loaded cabin went up, forty crates of bread, Sabrina Vedd's. She stood at the lower station with her arms folded and watched it go as if it had been rude to her bread. Ines signed the commissioning sheet under the inspector's name, and not before him.

On Friday the board met in the hall. Sabrina Vedd spoke for four minutes, which was one more than she had been given. Dr Orsolya stood after her with a letter, and read it in the same dry, careful voice in which he had asked for a forty-first fact.

**Dr Orsolya**  
I diagnosed forty children with what I could not hear. I withdraw my recommendation of the transfer, and the sentence in the draft that calls it a placement. The offer of observation at Dessau stands for any family that asks for it, in any month, and no child goes on a notice of mine. If in three weeks a family still wants it, the request is theirs to make, and I will sign it.

The board voted to shelve the transfer and to keep the Dessau offer for any family that asked. It was not unanimous and nobody pretended it was. Two members thought the doctor had given way too fast, said so aloud, and were thanked for it.

scenes.title: A Little Hill
paragraphs: *The little room, High Wendel school · three weeks later, the first snow*
The snow came down without wind, and the cabin crossed it, red and slow, humming in a register that had dropped into the walls of the world.
The teacher asked again whether anyone would like the window opened. A girl in the second row raised her chin.

Nessa said li. It rose, small and bright, a little hill, and Illuminara, who sat at the back with her hearing turned all the way up and her hands in her lap, discovered that she had stopped breathing.

Daan opened the window. The cold came in, and the sound of the car, and a boy at the back said li with a fall in it that was unmistakably a complaint about the cold. The room laughed. Nobody laughed at a river.

Thirty-eight of the forty were speaking by then, at school and at home, loudly and sloppily and without pause. Two were not. For Wilma and Teo the silence had a second root, as Dr Orsolya had said it might, and the wall had been hiding it. Now that the channel was clean he could hear it, and he went to the little room on Tuesdays and sat with them and asked them for nothing. Dessau stood in the minutes as an offer. Wilma's mother had asked to see the place, and had come home and chosen Tuesdays instead; Teo's parents had not asked. Nobody called it failure.
At the gate Sabrina Vedd was waiting in her freight-shed jacket. Nessa, who had been talking for forty minutes without drawing breath, stopped in the middle of a sentence about a bucket.

**Nessa**  
Li.
It was a little hill. Sabrina said li back, badly, in the wrong register, and her daughter corrected her all the way down the road.
Illuminara watched from the gate. The cabin crossed above them, humming low, in a register no six-year-old needed, and a hill, a small one, went on up and down the road in the snow.

critic_line: Illuminara learns from Nessa that the children are speaking clearly outside the school, then helps Ines and Dr Orsolya test the cable car's masking note under a signed, reconstructible protocol; Ines freely repairs the mechanism under independent safety commissioning, the board shelves compulsory transfer, thirty-eight children speak again, and the two whose silence has another root receive patient local care and a voluntary specialist option without being called failures.

shared_strengths: A fresh, concrete mystery with a satisfying, fair-play solution (tonal language masked by gearbox hum), a humane tone, good dialogue, and an emotional payoff in the little hill. The preregistered-protocol card and engineering detail are dense and may slow some readers, and the resolution is tidy.

A warm, intelligent mystery turns acoustics into an emotionally legible problem, with vivid dialogue, fair-minded adults, and an earned, restrained resolution. The lengthy experimental protocol and engineering certification slow the middle, but the children’s tonal language, the little-hill motif, and the refusal to treat the two remaining silent children as failures should linger.
shared_reservations: No separate improvement instruction was provided beyond Claude’s attributed reader explanation.

translation_sl.title: TIHA ŠOLA V KRAJU HIGH WENDEL
translation_sl.deck: Štirideset otrok, mlajših od devet let, je v šoli v kraju High Wendel prenehalo govoriti, žičnica, klinika in glasovanje odbora pa vsak po svoje trdijo, da vedo zakaj. Illuminara ne more slišati tistega, česar se otrok odloči ne izreči, zato zastavi vprašanje, ki ga ni še nihče: ali je kanal, po katerem govorijo, čist?
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov v petih dneh in prvi sneg tri tedne pozneje: šolska vrata, kjer se mati in zdravnik ne strinjata, učilnica, kjer junakinja postane slaba učenka, strojnica, kjer inženirka zahteva, naj ji pokažejo zvok, vnaprej zapisan opoldanski preizkus, noč popravila z navedenimi omejitvami in varnostnim pregledom ter da, ki se vzpne kakor hrib.

scenes.title: Pet dni
paragraphs: *High Wendel, šolska vrata · ponedeljek, deset čez osem, štiri dni pred glasovanjem odbora*

Žičnica je vsakih enajst minut prečkala nebo nad vrati, rdeča kabina ob tankih oblakih, in nihče v kraju High Wendel ni več pogledal navzgor. Februarja je plaz za enajst dni zaprl prelaz. Žičnico, ki so jo odprli aprila, so zgradili zato, da nič nikoli več ne bi odrezalo mesta od sveta.
Ženska v jakni iz tovornega skladišča je stala pri vratih s šestletnico za roko in je ni izpustila, ko je zazvonil zvonec.

**Sabrina**  
Sem Sabrina Vedd. Šest dni na teden pakiram kruh, ki gre gor s to žičnico, zato ne mislite, da sem prišla prosit, naj jo izklopite.

**Sabrina**  
Marca je ta tukaj pred zajtrkom na štirideset načinov rekla li. Zdaj me pogleda in naredi svoj obraz. To je vse. Naredi svoj obraz.

**Illuminara**  
Povejte mi enega od teh štiridesetih.

**Sabrina**  
Da. Na koncu gre navzgor, kakor da kliče psa.
Deklica je pogledala v tla, vrata in Illuminaro ter ni rekla ničesar. Ime ji je bilo Nessa. Imela je materino brado.
Suh moški z mapo pod pazduho je čakal na premor in ga izkoristil.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Pavel Orsolya, šolski zdravnik. Rad bi bil kratek in vljuden, eno od tega mi bo uspelo. Štirideset otrok, mlajših od devet let, prav vsak od njih je v istih šestih tednih v razredu utihnil. Medicinska sestra jim je pregledala sluh in vseh štirideset je pregled opravilo. Logopedinja, ki prvi ponedeljek v mesecu prihaja iz Dessaua, jih je videla devet in ni našla ničesar v ušesu, ustih ali jeziku. Februarja je zdrsnila gora in prelaz je bil zaprt enajst dni. Otroci zadržujejo strah, dokler ga ni varno odložiti. April je bil prvi varni mesec.

**Sabrina**  
Doma govorijo. Malo. V zadnjih sobah, pri zaprtih vratih.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Prav to strah naredi z varno sobo. In tu je škoda, ki jo poskušam preprečiti. Bralna preverjanja bodo čez šest tednov. Otrok, ki ne bere na glas, ponavlja razred, sedemletnik, ki ponavlja, pa se nauči, da šola ni zanj. Klinika v Dessauu jih lahko opazuje vsak dan. Jaz jih ne morem, terapevtka pa zmore enkrat na mesec.

**Illuminara**  
Ali se mora z Dessauom strinjati vsaka družina?

**Dr Orsolya**  
Po mojem predlogu da, vprašali bi tudi vsakega otroka, kadar ga je mogoče vprašati. V petek odbor glasuje o osnutku, ki govori o namestitvi in obvestilu staršem. Teh besed nisem napisal in jih nisem spravil ven.

**Sabrina**  
Odvzeli bi jo z obvestilom.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Morda. Zato bom v petek nasprotoval temu besedilu in priporočil opazovanje. Oboje. To je nepriljubljeno stališče in ga zagovarjam.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj bi vam pokazalo, da se motite?
Vprašanje je pretehtal, kakor da je pacient.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Enainštirideseto dejstvo, ki ga strah ne more pojasniti. Iskal sem ga in ga nisem našel. Če ga najdete, mi ga prinesite pred petkom in ga bom prebral. Ne bom užival.

**Illuminara**  
Rada bi en dan sedela v njihovem razredu in jih ne prosila za nič.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Ne prosite jih za nič. To bom z veseljem podpisal.

scenes.title: Slaba učenka
paragraphs: *Mala učilnica, šola v kraju High Wendel · ponedeljek, pol enajstih*

Illuminara se je čez noč naučila vseh štiri tisoč besed wennščine. Toni so bili druga stvar. Ton ni nekaj, kar veš; je nekaj, kar narediš z glasom, in en sam zlog li je pomenil reko, če je ostal raven, žalost, če je padel, in da, če se je dvignil. Njen glas je zmogel vse, kar je bilo težava. Ni imel navad, na katere bi lahko zvalila krivdo.

Preden je sedla, je naredila nekaj, česar navadno ni. Sluh je zmanjšala na razpon običajnega učitelja, da ne bi bila edina v prostoru, ki sliši tisto, česar otroci ne morejo. Bilo je, kakor da bi hodila z roko čez eno oko.
V sobi je bilo toplo od peči. Dvanajst otrok je sedelo na nizkih klopeh v tišini, tako lepo vzgojeni, da je bila skoraj vljudnost. Nessa Vedd je sedela v drugi vrsti.
Učitelj, tihi mož po imenu Daan, je vprašal, ali bi kdo rad odprl okno. Nessa je dvignila brado in izrekla en zlog z majhnim svetlim dvigom na koncu.
Illuminara je slišala reka. Ravno in plosko, besedo za nekaj, česar v sobi ni bilo.

Tudi učitelj je slišal reka. Nagnil je glavo in ji prijazno povedal, da tu ni reke, nekateri drugi pa so se mu nasmehnili. Bil je zelo prijazen nasmeh. Nessin obraz se je zaprl kakor vrata na tečaju in tisto dopoldne ni rekla ničesar več.
*Rekla je da,* je pomislila Illuminara. *Videla sem, kako se je njena brada dvignila. Slišala sem nekaj drugega.*
Še štirikrat pred opoldanskim zvoncem je otrok poskusil izreči besedo in dobil odgovor, ki se z njo ni ujemal, in vsakič je otrok nekoliko dlje gledal v tla.
Opoldne so stekli na vrt pod šolo in tišina se je razlomila kakor reka, ko odnese led.

Vrt je bil glasen. Poln je bil li, ki so se dvigali, padali in ostajali ravni, vrženi od otroka do otroka kakor žoga, za njimi pa so se podili celi stavki. Nessa je stala na zidu spodaj in nekemu fantu ukazovala glede vedra.
Illuminara je sedla na kamen ob njej in kot vljudna gostja poskusila besedo. Rekla je li, mislila da, in pustila glasu iti tja, kamor je menila, da mora iti da.
Nessa je odložila vedro in se tako zasmejala, da se je morala prijeti zidu.

**Nessa**  
To je žalost. Rekli ste, da ste žalostni. Da gre gor. Gor, kakor hrib.

**Illuminara**  
Pokaži mi, kateri hrib.

**Nessa**  
Majhen hrib. Kot babičin, za cerkvijo. Ne gora. Vi delate goro.
Illuminara je naredila majhen hrib. Nessa ga je ocenila z glavo, nagnjeno vstran, rekla, da bo šlo, in na dolgo pojasnila, zakaj je vedro njeno.
*Tu spodaj govorijo. Pri vratih se ustavijo.* Ta stavek je odnesla po vrtni poti kakor polno skodelico.

Pri šolskih vratih je sluh odprla do konca in tla so spregovorila. Skozi kamen se je dvigal en sam raven ton, nič glasnejši od kotlička v zadnjem delu hiše in enakomeren kakor zadržan dih. Ležal je natanko tako visoko kot glas šestletnika. Pod vsako besedo, izrečeno v tisti stavbi, je narisal ravno črto, ravna črta pa zveni kakor reka.

scenes.title: Pokažite mi zvok
paragraphs: *Zgornja postaja, strojnica · ponedeljek, pol treh*

Ines Kallas je žičnico zasnovala za kuhinjsko mizo v dolini, ki je ni hotela financirati, in Illuminaro je gledala tako, kot je gledala natrgano žico. Za njo se je vrtelo veliko pogonsko kolo, ogromno in skoraj neslišno.

**Ines**  
Torej ste vi tista, ki pravi, da moj stroj požira otroke.

**Illuminara**  
Mislim, da vaš stroj poje, in mislim, da otroški glasovi živijo natanko tam, kjer poje on.

**Ines**  
Moj stroj je tih. Enainpetdeset decibelov pri šolskem zidu. To je knjižnica.

**Illuminara**  
Knjižnica ni ton. Vaš menjalnik ima pri potovalni hitrosti zobniški ton okoli tristo deset hercev in drugega pri šeststo dvajsetih. Moški glas leži pod njim. Glas šestletnika leži prav na njem. V wennščini je drsenje glasu navzgor ali navzdol celotna razlika med da in žalostjo, drsenje čez enakomeren ton iste višine pa je črta s svinčnikom na s svinčnikom sivem zidu. V tej sobi rečejo da, drugi pa slišijo reka. Nikjer drugje.

**Ines**  
Pri enainpetdesetih decibelih.

**Illuminara**  
Ne skriva ga glasnost. Istost ga.
Ines ni rekla nič toliko časa, kolikor ga je kabina potrebovala, da je zapustila postajo.

**Ines**  
Hočete, da ustavim edino cesto, ki jo to mesto ima, na podlagi teorije o zvoku. Februarja sem bila na prelazu z lopato. Vem, koliko stane, ko je cesta zaprta. Pokažite mi zvok.

**Illuminara**  
Ne prosim vas, da jo ustavite. Prosim vas, da mi dovolite pokazati, in da najprej zapišemo, kaj bi dokazalo, da se motim.

**Ines**  
Zapisano kam?

**Illuminara**  
Na kartico, ki jo podpišemo vse tri, preden kdorkoli sliši eno samo besedo.

**Ines**  
Prav. In sama opravim svoj merilni prehod s svojim instrumentom. Nobenih ušes ne jemljem za frekvenco, še najmanj vaših.
Spektralni zapis je odnesla k mizi in ga pridržala pod svetilko. Na njem sta stali dve ozki, čisti konici pri tristo devet in šeststo osemnajst.

**Ines**  
Konica ni otrok.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. To je druga polovica. Med opoldanskim premorom žičnico zadržijo zaradi pregleda vrvi in dvajset minut ni tona. Rada bi predvajala iste besede v obeh polovicah in videla, kdo sliši kaj.

**Ines**  
Dvajset minut je vse, kar dobite. Ne enaindvajset.

scenes.title: Opoldanski premor
paragraphs: *Šolska dvorana · torek, dve minuti pred poldnevom*
Kartico so prejšnji večer podpisali trije ljudje in jo zapečatili v kuverto na klavirju. Illuminara jo je prebrala na glas, da nihče ne bi mogel reči, da njenih pogojev ni slišal.

*Osem poslušalcev v dveh štiričlanskih skupinah, v dveh sobah. Štiriindvajset posnetkov, dvanajst otroških in dvanajst odraslih, ki izgovarjajo iste besede, je razdeljenih v Nabor A in Nabor B, v vsakem je šest otrok in šest odraslih. Prva skupina sliši Nabor A ob delujočem pogonu pred poldnevom in Nabor B ob ustavljenem pogonu. Druga skupina sliši Nabor A ob ustavljenem pogonu in Nabor B ob delujočem pogonu po premoru. Tako vsak glas ocenijo štirje poslušalci ob delujočem pogonu in drugi štirje ob ustavljenem, nihče pa istega glasu ne sliši dvakrat. Glas je v danem stanju napačno slišan, kadar trije od štirih poslušalcev zapišejo besedo, ki ni tista, ki jo je govorec želel izreči, kakor je na hrbtno stran zapisala mati, ki je prosila za preizkus. Če je ob delujočem pogonu napačno slišanih več kot tri od dvanajstih otroških glasov, ob ustavljenem pa največ eden, glasovi odraslih pa so obakrat slišani pravilno, temu rečemo prekrivanje. Če ne, Illuminara to pove in odneha. Dr Orsolya dodaja: to ne izključuje strahu. Ines dodaja: nič od tega se ne dotika žičnice.*

Štirinajst družin so prosili za glasovni posnetek iz pomladi, preden je bila žičnica, in najprej so vprašali vsakega otroka. Dva sta rekla ne in nihče ju ni vprašal drugič. Dvanajst tistih, ki so se strinjali, je bilo v kuverti poleg dvanajstih odraslih, ki so izgovarjali iste besede. Nessa je materi v zadnji sobi povedala, da lahko njen da-psu predvajajo enkrat, in sedela je v zadnjem delu dvorane s prekrižanimi rokami. Nihče je ni prosil, naj izreče eno samo besedo.

Šest staršev, Ines in Dr Orsolya je sedelo z listki: Prva skupina v dvorani, Druga skupina v mali učilnici čez hodnik, v vsaki sobi po en zvočnik. Illuminara ni glasovala. Vrstni red vsakega nabora je izžrebala iz klobuka in vsak poslušalec je zapisal reka, žalost ali da.

Prvi sklop Prve skupine je potekal ob delujoči žičnici. Opoldne se je kabina z dolgim vzdihom ustavila na postaji in ton je ugasnil v tleh kakor izpuščen zadržan dih. Illuminara je začutila, kako je izginil iz njene prsnice. *Če se listki vrnejo ravni,* je pomislila, *sem teden štiridesetih otrok postavila na domnevo.* Dvajset minut premora sta obe sobi poslušali hkrati, Prva skupina Nabor B in Druga skupina Nabor A.

Ob dvajset čez dvanajst je žičnica odpeljala, ton se je vrnil v tla, Druga skupina pa je začela svoj sklop ob delujočem pogonu, Nabor B. Listke je preštela dvakrat, z Ines in Dr Orsolyo ob ramenih, in rezultate prebrala v vrstnem redu, ki ga je obljubila.

**Illuminara**  
Otroci, pogon deluje: sedem od dvanajstih glasov napačno slišanih. Otroci, pogon miruje: nobeden. Odrasli, deluje: nobeden. Odrasli, miruje: nobeden.
Nihče ni spregovoril. Kabina je prečkala okno in nadaljevala navzgor po gori.

**Ines**  
Vrstni red.

**Illuminara**  
Prva skupina je najprej slišala delujočo žičnico in nato ustavljeno, Druga skupina pa v obratnem vrstnem redu. Vsak nabor so slišali v obeh stanjih, različni ljudje v nasprotnem vrstnem redu, in listki vsake skupine kažejo isti razcep: ob delujočem pogonu so slišali narobe, ob ustavljenem čisto. Tu so njihovi listi.
Položila jih je na klavir poleg kuverte. Ines jih je brala tako, kot bi brala zvar.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Sedem. In nobeden. Potem sem štiri mesece poslušal štirideset otrok skozi napačen zid.

**Illuminara**  
Ali skozi zid, za katerega nihče ni vedel, da je tam.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Rad bi, da bi me to potolažilo. Za zdaj me ne. To mi ne pove, ali jih je tudi strah.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Tega ne moremo vedeti, dokler zid ne izgine. Potem boste slišali, kar ostane, in vi boste tisti, ki bo na to odgovoril.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Potem ga podrite. Jaz bom ugotovil, kaj je ostalo.
Ines je izpolnila svoj list kakor vsi drugi in zdaj strmela v svoj zapis.

**Ines**  
Tristo devet. Dve leti sem temu tonu rekla gladek. Ta menjalnik sem uglaševala z ušesi odraslega.
Papir je prepognila na štiri dele.

**Ines**  
Popravila ga bom. Ne zahvaljujte se mi.

scenes.title: Štirje odstotki
paragraphs: *Zgornja postaja, strojnica · sreda ponoči, deset čez deset*

Ines je mesto prosila za noč. Enajst ur brez njegove edine ceste je bila cena in to je povedala najprej. Delala je z zadržano žičnico od zadnje večerne vožnje do devetih zjutraj in s petčlansko ekipo, med delom pa je vse pojasnjevala, ker se je odločila, da mesta ne bo popravilo nič, česar ne bi moglo razumeti.

**Ines**  
Tri stvari. Izolacijski nosilec pod menjalnikom, da skala ne prenaša več tona po grebenu navzgor. Uglašeni dušilnik na ohišju za sam ton. In štiri odstotke manjša potovalna hitrost, ker so šolska tla boben, ki odmeva pri tristo deset, in rada bi, da ton prispe tja, kjer bobna ni.

**Illuminara**  
Koliko stanejo štirje odstotki?

**Ines**  
Vožnja traja osemintrideset minut. Štirje odstotki so minuto in pol. Dobite to in niti sekunde več.

**Ines**  
In tu so moje omejitve, da se nihče ne bo spraševal. Napetosti, zavore in vrvi se ne dotaknem ne zaradi vas, ne zaradi odbora, ne zaradi Boga. Nosilci in hitrost so moji. In to vrne stari nosilec: sklopka zunaj proizvajalčeve meje poravnave, menjalnik, ki se trese močneje kot lani, ali žičnica, ki za ustavitev potrebuje meter več. Ena sama od teh treh stvari in togi nosilec gre še nocoj nazaj, vi pa ste lahko vsi jezni name.

**Illuminara**  
Ne bi hotela, da naredite kaj drugega.

Ob šestih so opravili merilne prehode, njenega in tistega dolinskega inšpektorja. Ponoči se je pripeljal s termovko in nezaupanjem do navdušenja ter prišel preverit, da se popravilo ni dotaknilo tistega, česar se ne sme. Zapisa sta ležala drug čez drugega kakor podpis in njegova kopija. Ton pri šolskem zidu je bil nižji za šestindvajset decibelov in nihče ga ni mogel najti v tleh.

Nato je prišel del, ki ga nihče ne bi dal v zgodbo. Sklopka je bila znotraj omejitve. Menjalnik se je tresel manj kot leto prej. Ob sedmih je žičnica peljala gor prazna in prazna prišla dol. Ob osmih je Ines opravila zasilno ustavitev iz polne hitrosti s kabino, naloženo z vrečami peska, in inšpektor, ki je pričakoval napako, je zapisal zavorno pot ter jo pogledal, kakor da mu nekaj dolguje: znotraj potrdila, s pol metra rezerve. Ob devetih je šla navzgor prva naložena kabina, štirideset zabojev kruha Sabrine Vedd. Stala je na spodnji postaji s prekrižanimi rokami in gledala, kako gre, kakor da je bila nesramna do njenega kruha. Ines je podpisala zapisnik o zagonu pod inšpektorjevim imenom in ne pred njim.

V petek se je odbor sestal v dvorani. Sabrina Vedd je govorila štiri minute, eno več, kot so ji jih dali. Dr Orsolya je za njo vstal s pismom in ga prebral z istim suhim, previdnim glasom, s katerim je prosil za enainštirideseto dejstvo.

**Dr Orsolya**  
Štiridesetim otrokom sem postavil diagnozo na podlagi tistega, česar nisem mogel slišati. Umikam svoje priporočilo za premestitev in stavek v osnutku, ki temu pravi namestitev. Ponudba opazovanja v Dessauu ostaja za vsako družino, ki zanjo zaprosi, v kateremkoli mesecu, in noben otrok ne gre tja z mojim obvestilom. Če bo čez tri tedne družina to še želela, bo prošnja njihova in podpisal jo bom.

Odbor je izglasoval, da premestitev umaknejo in ponudbo Dessaua ohranijo za vsako družino, ki zanjo zaprosi. Glasovanje ni bilo soglasno in nihče se ni pretvarjal, da je. Dva člana sta menila, da je zdravnik popustil prehitro, to povedala na glas in za to so se jima zahvalili.

scenes.title: Majhen hrib
paragraphs: *Mala učilnica, šola v kraju High Wendel · tri tedne pozneje, prvi sneg*
Sneg je padal brez vetra in kabina ga je prečkala, rdeča in počasna, brneč v registru, ki se je spustil v zidove sveta.
Učitelj je znova vprašal, ali bi kdo rad odprl okno. Deklica v drugi vrsti je dvignila brado.
Nessa je rekla li. Dvignil se je, majhen in svetel, majhen hrib, Illuminara, ki je sedela zadaj s sluhom, odprtim do konca, in rokami v naročju, pa je odkrila, da je nehala dihati.
Daan je odprl okno. Vstopili so mraz, zvok žičnice in deček zadaj, ki je rekel li s padcem, ki je bil nedvomno pritožba nad mrazom. Soba se je zasmejala. Nihče se ni smejal reki.

Osemintrideset od štiridesetih je takrat že govorilo, v šoli in doma, glasno, neurejeno in brez premora. Dva nista. Pri Wilmi in Teu je imela tišina še drugo korenino, kakor je Dr Orsolya rekel, da jo morda ima, zid pa jo je skrival. Zdaj ko je bil kanal čist, jo je lahko slišal, in ob torkih je hodil v malo učilnico, sedel z njima ter ju ni prosil za nič. Dessau je v zapisniku ostal kot ponudba. Wilmina mati je prosila, da bi si kraj ogledala, se vrnila domov in izbrala torke; Teovi starši niso prosili. Nihče temu ni rekel neuspeh.
Pri vratih je čakala Sabrina Vedd v jakni iz tovornega skladišča. Nessa, ki je štirideset minut govorila, ne da bi zajela sapo, se je ustavila sredi stavka o vedru.

**Nessa**  
Li.
Bil je majhen hrib. Sabrina je rekla li nazaj, slabo, v napačnem registru, hči pa jo je popravljala vso pot po cesti navzdol.
Illuminara je gledala od vrat. Kabina je prečkala nebo nad njima, brneč nizko, v registru, ki ga noben šestletnik ni potreboval, in hrib, majhen, je v snegu nadaljeval gor in dol po cesti.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara od Nesse izve, da otroci zunaj šole govorijo jasno, nato Ines in dr. Orsolyi pomaga preizkusiti prekrivajoči ton žičnice s podpisanim, ponovljivim postopkom; Ines prostovoljno popravi mehanizem pod neodvisnim varnostnim nadzorom, odbor umakne obvezno premestitev, osemintrideset otrok znova spregovori, dva, katerih tišina ima drugo korenino, pa prejmeta potrpežljivo lokalno oskrbo in prostovoljno možnost specialista, ne da bi ju kdo imenoval neuspeh.
